transcript:
Meeting Header: Date: 2026-10-29 15:00 UTC | Duration: 54 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE); Clara Zhou (Empire Retail, Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Platform Engineer), Priya Patel (Security Lead)

Summary:
Jordan opens, quick intro, goal is to align on POC success criteria, sizing, benchmark plan and decide between Hosted/Dedicated/Private modes. Customer emphasized latency-sensitive inference for personalization and strict data privacy for user data. Discussion covers throughput targets, token distributions, quantization tolerance, security and timeline to a pilot.

Topics:
- Success criteria (latency p95 < 120ms for short prompts; throughput 200 QPS steady; cost per 1k tokens target)
- Workload sizing and token distributions
- Benchmark plan and metrics (p95 latency, p99, throughput, GPU utilization, cost/unit)
- Deployment options tradeoffs (Hosted, Dedicated, Private/VPC/on-prem)
- Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, SSO)
- Timeline and next steps

Action items (short list here, full items in metadata): Jordan to send pricing, Samira to share benchmark scripts, Marcus to provide traffic trace, Priya to enumerate compliance items.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for carving time, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, with Samira and Luis on the call from our solutions engineering team. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Clara (Empire): Good, thanks, Jordan. Hi Samira, Luis. We're excited to get this scoped. I'll probably hand off some of the infra details to Marcus for the heavy lifting.
[00:12] Marcus (Customer): Yeah hi all, Marcus here. We've got a big personalization surface for the product recs, probably lots of short prompts — average prompt 35 tokens, responses ~120 tokens.
[00:19] Samira (Redwood SE): Cool, that token distribution's helpful. When you say personalization, is latency for the inline recs a hard constraint? Like do you need <100ms p95, or is 150ms acceptable?
[00:30] Clara: Ideally we want p95 under 120ms for the short paths. For background batch reranks we can tolerate higher latency.
[00:36] Luis (Redwood SE): Okay that's useful. For short prompts that implies smaller sequence lengths but high QPS. Do you have a sense of peak QPS vs steady state?
[00:45] Marcus: Peak around 400 QPS sustained for 2–3 minutes during marketing bursts; steady is 180–220 QPS. Our SLA with clients expects 99.9% availability during business hours.
[00:58] Priya (Customer): And on the security front we need SOC2 type II, SSO via SAML, audit logs retention for 90 days, and keys managed in our KMS, not held by vendors. Also data residency in EU for EU customers.
[01:12] Jordan: Great, that's the level of detail we need. Quick framing: we have three hosting paths — Hosted Redwood API (fastest onboarding), Dedicated reserved capacity (predictable throughput, isolated GPU pools), and Private (VPC or on-prem with customer managed KMS). Each has tradeoffs in latency, cost, and operational overhead.
[01:30] Clara: Can you give a concrete example of tradeoffs? We want to see why we might pick Dedicated vs Hosted.
[01:36] Samira: Sure. Hosted is lowest friction — you hit the API, we do routing, caching, and manage KV cache. For your latency target, Hosted can often hit 120ms p95 for lighter models or when we use prefix caching. But for sustained peaks of 400 QPS, hosted cost can be higher and cold-start variability might be an issue. Dedicated gets you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput with lower unit cost and tighter latency SLOs; Private gives you full control for KMS and on-prem constraints but requires more integration and a longer timeline to stand up.
[02:05] Marcus: So are there GPU types you recommend? We're considering a Llama-2 style quantized model, around 13B.
[02:11] Luis: For 13B quantized 4-bit, on A10s or similar we can get good latency; for tighter p95 you'd consider H100-style machines. We'll propose specific instance types in the benchmark plan.
[02:22] Speaker 1: (inaudible) ... sorry just dropped —
[02:25] Samira: No worries. One important step is determining acceptable quality loss if we quantize to int4 or use quantization-aware kernels. Do you have a test suite for quality regression or hold out evals?
[02:37] Clara: We have a small evaluation set for top-line personalization metrics — we can share a few prompt-response pairs and acceptance thresholds. We care mostly about nDCG on reranks and semantic similarity for recs.
[02:47] Jordan: Perfect. So proposed success criteria from Redwood: 1) Functional parity on sample eval set (tolerance threshold we'll align on), 2) Latency p95 <= 120ms for short-paths and p99 <= 350ms for tail, 3) Sustained throughput 180–220 QPS with peaks to 400, 4) Cost target — goal to be below $X per 1k tokens (we'll compute), 5) Security checklist satisfied (SOC2 or equivalent docs, KMS integration for Private option).
[03:15] Marcus: That lines up. For cost target, we have a budget cap for inference of X per month, but we'll need a per-token estimate to model at scale.
[03:23] Jordan: We'll provide an estimated cost table after we have the benchmark numbers and token distribution. For POC — we typically run a 48–72 hour benchmark that includes steady-state and spike tests, capture GPU utilization, throughput, and variance — we'll also run a latency SLO test with synthetic traffic that mirrors your trace.
[03:41] Clara: Are we doing benchmarks on Hosted or Dedicated? Or both?
[03:45] Samira: We recommend starting with Hosted to validate model performance and quality quickly, then run the heavier Dedicated benchmarks to capture scaling and cost delta. If Private is required for compliance, we can provision a VPC deployment and run the same harness there, but that adds about 2–3 weeks of setup.
[03:59] Priya: The KMS requirement — we can't have keys in vendor custody. Does Hosted support customer-managed KMS? I thought that was only Private.
[04:07] Luis: Current Hosted model supports envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in some regions — but full KMS isolation with HSM-level controls is only available with Private on-prem or VPC with dedicated KMS. We'll put exact capabilities and docs in the security pack.
[04:20] Marcus: For the benchmark harness, what inputs do you need? We can provide a production traffic trace but will scrub PII.
[04:26] Samira: Ideal: 24h trace with timestamps, request latency arrival distribution, prompt lengths, and token distribution. Also a sample of worst-case long prompts so we can validate tail behavior. We'll provide a repo with load scripts to replay traffic as well as a local harness for you to run.
[04:42] Jordan: On timelines realistically: If we get the trace by 11/04 and Samira shares harness by 10/31, we can run a first 48h benchmark in week of 11/08 and have a findings deck by 11/12. Private deployment would push pilot readiness to late November depending on network approvals.
[05:00] Clara: That timeline works, our procurement window is late Nov so we'd like results before that.
[05:05] Speaker 2 (Customer): Quick question about failover — what happens if Dedicated capacity is exhausted? We can't have service loss.
[05:12] Samira: We support automatic fallbacks — routing policies can fallback to compatible model variants in Hosted or burst to shared capacity, with a configurable SLA and cost controls. We'll show sample policies.
[05:24] Marcus: For observability, we need per-route latency breakdowns and token-level billing for forecasting.
[05:30] Luis: That's in Redwood Console — we can give you sample dashboards and token breakdown per model/route. We also have tracing hooks you can plug into your APM.
[05:39] Clara: Any gotchas around prompt caching / prefix caching with personalization keys? We have dynamic user prefixes that reduce cache hit rate.
[05:46] Samira: If user prefixes are highly unique, cache hit rates drop — our recommended pattern is a hybrid approach: prefix KV cache for common patterns + short-term local cache for per-user tokens. That reduces cost without sacrificing freshness. We'll run experiments to measure hit rate given your trace.
[06:02] Priya: About audit logs — we need immutable logs for 90 days and the ability to export them to our SIEM. Is that doable in Hosted?
[06:10] Jordan: Hosted supports audit logs and exports — retention tiers vary, enterprise retention options available as add-on. Private gives you direct control to pipe logs to your SIEM.
[06:19] Clara: Let's talk benchmarks specifics — what metrics will you report and how?
[06:23] Samira: We'll report: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, throughput (RPS/QPS), GPU utilization, memory/KV cache hit rate, cost per 1k tokens, error rates, and quality regression on your eval set. We'll deliver CSVs, a deck, and raw perf traces.
[06:40] Marcus: For cost per 1k tokens, will you include network egress and infra amortization?
[06:46] Luis: We'll include compute and operational overhead; egress is usually a separate line item but we'll estimate it based on average response sizes.
[06:53] Speaker 3 (Customer): Could you also show a side-by-side cost table for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private at our projected volumes?
[06:58] Jordan: Absolutely — that's part of the pricing + cost model spreadsheet we'll send. It will show unit cost, expected monthly bill at steady-state, and 95th-percentile spike scenarios.
[07:09] Clara: One more question — do you run A/B tests for model rollouts? We want canary with automatic rollback on quality regression.
[07:16] Samira: Yes, Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies triggered by eval regressions or latency anomalies.
[07:24] Marcus: Ok that helps. Security-wise, Priya will need the SOC2 report and an architecture diagram for VPC peering.
[07:31] Priya: Also a data flow diagram showing where keys live and log flows.
[07:36] Jordan: We'll attach our security pack and a VPC diagram. Note that for a Private VPC deploy we'll run a pre-flight checklist with networking and firewall rules — usually 2–3 weeks to provision.
[07:48] Clara: What's the recommended model size again for latency/cost tradeoff? We're open to 7B vs 13B.
[07:54] Luis: 7B will be cheaper and faster with modest quality drop; 13B usually gives better personalization but at higher cost. We'll run both in the benchmark harness and show tradeoffs.
[08:05] Jordan: To recap real quick: success criteria include quality parity on your eval set, p95 latency under 120ms for short-paths, sustained 180–220 QPS, cost targets to be validated, and security signoffs. Actions: Jordan send pricing, Samira share harness, Marcus provide traces, Priya list compliance items. Benchmark week targeted 11/08 with findings by 11/12.
[08:28] Clara: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:31] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the links and invite for the benchmark slot.
[08:35] Meeting ends
